raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer, thinking through the season...*

---

Forty years on this land and I still sit down with my wife in late September to talk through what we're going to do. It's just the two of us now — our son is up in Baoding working construction. She helps where she can but her knees make the cotton picking hard. That's the part I worry about most.

My 10.1 mu, I split it the same as last few years: 6 mu for the wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu cotton over on the west side of the field. The wheat-maize is my steady income. The cotton, honestly, some of my neighbors have dropped it, but I've been growing it since I was young and I still know how to do it. Price was 6.2 yuan per jin last year at the village depot. Not great, not terrible.

**Wheat (6 mu, planting now in October):**

I watch when Lao Zhang across the lane plants. He's got the same soil type as me — heavy loam, decent water holding. We usually go in around October 10th or so, sometimes a few days later if it's still warm. Early planting and you get too much growth before winter, the aphids love it.

I hire someone to rotary till after the maize comes off. My back can't manage the big equipment anymore. Then I spread the base fertilizer myself — I use compound fertilizer, the 45% stuff, about 40 kg per mu. That's what the village extension station told us five or six years ago and it's worked fine. Then about 15 kg of urea per mu. I split the urea: half at planting mixed into the base, half topdress at jointing in March if the leaves look pale. Sometimes I skip the topdress on part of the field if money is tight in spring.

Irrigation: I do winter water in November or December — important for overwintering. Then jointing water in March. Then heading water in April or May. If it doesn't rain at grain fill I'll do a fourth. Groundwater pumping costs me about 25-30 yuan per mu per time, so I don't irrigate for nothing.

Yield: I got 410 kg/mu last year. Year before was 450. Hoping for 420 or so.

**Maize (6 mu, same field, right after wheat harvest in June):**

This is the rushed part. Wheat comes off around June 10th or 12th, I need to get maize in by the 15th at the latest or I lose growing days. I hire the combine for wheat harvest and same day or next day I'm planting maize. I seed direct — no time for deep tillage, just a quick rotary pass if I can squeeze it, or sometimes straight no-till with a planter hired from the village machinery service.

I use hybrid seed, whatever the seed shop in the county town has that my neighbor tried last year. He got 520 kg/mu with Xianyu 335, so I'll probably do the same. Costs about 35 yuan/mu for seed.

Fertilizer: compound fertilizer as base, about 25 kg/mu, then topdress urea at big bell stage, maybe 15 kg/mu. Summer maize gets rain usually, so irrigation depends on weather. I irrigate at planting if soil is dry, and at tasseling if it's dry again. Maybe once or twice total.

Yield expectation: 460 kg/mu. Last year I got 490 but the rain was good.

**Cotton (4.1 mu, planted in late April):**

I plow this field in early April when the soil warms up. Cotton needs a clean seedbed. I plant around April 20th or so. I use the small plastic mulch film to keep moisture in and weeds down — I've done this for 15 years.

Base fertilizer: compound fertilizer 30 kg/mu, plus some extra potassium — cotton likes potassium. Then I topdress when the bolls start setting, another round of compound plus urea.

The spraying is the work. Cotton needs herbicide early, then insecticides when bollworm shows up in July and August. I spray myself with the backpack sprayer — 4.1 mu I can do in a day.

Picking is the problem. Three rounds of picking from September to October. My wife and I can do some but we'll need hired hands for the main picking, maybe 2-3 people for two days. I'll pay about 150 yuan per day per person. It adds up.

Lint yield: I'm expecting about 230 kg/mu. If the summer heat is good and no bad storm, maybe 240.

decision.reasoning_summary: I'm doing what I know works. The wheat-maize rotation on 6 mu is stable and I can mostly handle it myself except I hire a tractor for tillage and the combine for harvest — at 63 I'm not breaking my back on that. My biggest worry this year is the cotton picking: just two of us and my wife's knees aren't good, so I'll need to pay for hired pickers in September, which cuts into the margin. I kept cotton at 4.1 mu rather than expanding because of this labor constraint. On fertilizer I'm not changing much from last year — wheat got 16 kg nitrogen total split across two applications, which is what the extension station recommended and what Lao Zhang does too. Maize gets a bit less because summer rain usually helps. I won't borrow money for inputs if I can help it; I'll use what I saved from last autumn's sales.
